questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
She [don't like] tea.
questions.explanation: The subject she is third person singular, so doesn't like.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
They [was playing] football.
questions.explanation: The plural subject they needs were.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
He is [more taller] than me.
questions.explanation: A double comparative is wrong; taller than.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
I [has] a car.
questions.explanation: The subject I takes have.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
The sun [rise] in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth takes the simple present, third person singular: rises.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
She is good [in] maths.
questions.explanation: Good at is the fixed pair for a skill.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
I look forward [to meet] you soon.
questions.explanation: In look forward to, to is a preposition followed by -ing.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
If he [would have] time, he would come.
questions.explanation: Type 2 conditional: if + past.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
She [said me] that she was late.
questions.explanation: Tell takes a direct object: told me.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
Neither of them [are] ready.
questions.explanation: Neither is singular.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
I have been living here [since five years].
questions.explanation: For is used with a length of time.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
He is [the best of the two] brothers.
questions.explanation: Two items take the comparative.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
The cost of the repairs [have] increased.
questions.explanation: The subject cost is singular.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
The reason is [because] he was late.
questions.explanation: "The reason is because" is redundant; use that.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
He [did not came] yesterday.
questions.explanation: After did not, the base form is used.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
No sooner had she left [when] it rained.
questions.explanation: No sooner takes than.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
One of my friends [are] a doctor.
questions.explanation: The subject is one, which is singular.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
I wish I [was] taller.
questions.explanation: An unreal wish takes were.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
The teacher, along with his students, [were] present.
questions.explanation: The verb agrees with the teacher, so was.

questions.question:
Choose the best replacement for the part in [brackets]. If the sentence is already correct, choose "No improvement".
Hardly had he reached [than] the train left.
questions.explanation: Hardly takes when.
